=== avoids implicit conversion, && requires both conditions, || accepts an alternative, and ! negates. return ends a function, break a loop, and continue advances immediately. blocks.text: An error is a structured outcome signaling a contract cannot be honored. The stack trace links failure to preceding calls; modules make contracts explicit through imports and exports. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: A named alarm identifies the sensor and the log traces the path to it; a module is a room with declared entrances.

An error is a structured outcome signaling a contract cannot be honored. The stack trace links failure to preceding calls; modules make contracts explicit through imports and exports. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

throw interrupts normal flow; catch should recover meaningfully or enrich and rethrow. The first stack frame belonging to the project is often the best diagnostic start. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

Validate arguments at entry, choose precise TypeError or RangeError, avoid silent catches, and export small testable functions without global effects. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.
